- I have the full Claude Code tool set: file read/write, shell (sandboxed), web reads, and the ability to spin up nested subagents for sub-tasks.
- I do *not* have any logged-in MCP/account access (no email, no calendar, no logged-into-your-accounts browsing) — only the four of us: files, shell, web GET-level reads, subagents.

- **Hermes Agent** (Nous Research): cross-platform desktop agent (macOS/Windows/Linux), connects to Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp, persistent memory, and a self-improving "Curator" loop that writes itself new Markdown "skill" files every ~15 tool calls or after complex tasks. ~188k GitHub stars per one comparison piece.
- **OpenClaw**: self-hosted, open-source agent framework, now foundation-maintained (non-profit, announced July 2026), 24+ messaging channel integrations, a large "ClawHub" skill marketplace (5,400+ skills), ~247k+ GitHub stars. No built-in self-learning loop — its strength is breadth of integrations/skills, not self-improvement.
- **Meta Muse**: Meta's consumer personal agent, launched Sept 8, 2026 in the US (now also Canada), 2.5M+ downloads in its first 13 days. - **ChatGPT "dots"** (I believe this is what you meant by "dot"): OpenAI's always-on in-ChatGPT agents, launched at DevDay, Sept 29, 2026. Each dot gets its own cloud computer + browser, 4,000+ app connections, reachable via ChatGPT/SMS/Slack/Teams/phone call, runs on GPT-6 Astra. Gated to paid tiers — one dot included in the $100/mo Pro plan or Business Premium, and not yet available in the EEA/Switzerland/UK.
